text.p: Italian bond futures slipped towards the day's lows in late afternoon trading pressured by profit-taking and the weakening lira, dealers said.

Uncertainty over the possibility of an agreement on the planned mini-budget for 1997 between the Italian coalition government and the communists party continued to weigh on market sentiment, they added.
"There was no good reason to buy Italy today and plenty of reasons to stay. It was rather a technical trading session," one LIFFE trader said.

Dealers said if the government doesn't get Communist Refoundation support it could probably get support from the centre-right opposition -- but at what price. The government needs communist support in the lower house of parliament.
The bond market showed little reaction as the government won a confidence vote today on the last remaining chunk of the main 1997 financial budget.
Dealers added that bond markets were generally cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
